newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein stable, trade dull.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein stable, trade dull.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were stable in late trading on Wednesday after early falls but sentiment remained weak and demand limited, traders said.
They said olein was generally at 1,350-55 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, but quotes were also heard at 1,345 rupiah. Crude palm oil was last done at 1,145 rupiah/kg in Medan.
"Demand was scattered and buyers feel prices could go lower yet," one trader said. "Players have only been buying in small quantities and for immediate needs."
Traders attributed a steady decline in prices the past few weeks to weak consumer and industrial demand.
Traders said supply was expected to remain sufficient with the arrival of fresh shipments.
Data from Belawan Port showed that the MT Bobo left the port for Jakarta with 4,000 tonnes of olein on Sunday, a day after the MT Bumagh left for Jakarta with 4,200 tonnes of olein.
The MT Tirta Karsa was scheduled to sail to Semarang in Central Java on Wednesday with 2,150 tonnes of palm olein.

MT Kichen-Caribien would leave Belawan on Thursday for Pasir Gudang, Malaysia with 4,500 tonnes of olein, while the MV Pattaya Navee is scheduled to leave for Phuket on Friday with 5,000 tonnes of palm kernel expeller.
The MT Sinar Surya is to leave for Semarang with 1,400 tonnes of olein on Thursday, one day after the MV Tasik Mas left for the Central Java town with 2,105 tonnes of olein.
The data also showed that 9,000 tonnes of crude palm oil left for Dumai on Tuesday on board the MT Bunga Anggrek.
Another shipment of 12,500 tonnes of palm olein left the port for Singapore on board the G. Ordzhonnikloze on Tuesday.
